title: Understanding PCA
text: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to emphasize variation and bring out strong patterns in a dataset. It projects data onto new axes, called principal components, which are linear combinations of the original variables.

title: Interpreting Scatter Plots
text: Look at the scatter plot labeled (g.i). It shows a clear pattern. Consider how this pattern might relate to the principal components, pc1 and pc2.

title: Choosing the Correct Axis Label for (g.i)
text: Which principal component, pc1 or pc2, is likely represented on the x-axis of plot (g.i) based on the pattern observed?
